rows: Dutyholders must determine whether asbestos-containing materials may be present in relevant non-domestic premises.
The condition and location of known or presumed asbestos should be assessed.
An up-to-date record of asbestos location and condition should be maintained.
A written plan should describe how asbestos risks will be managed.
Information about asbestos should be provided to people liable to disturb it.
Materials should be monitored and actions reviewed over time.
Work that may disturb asbestos requires appropriate assessment, controls and competent contractors.
Unplanned damage or discovery should trigger immediate restriction, assessment and incident management.
An asbestos survey or register does not prove that every intrusive task is safe.
Conclusions require survey scope, material condition, task location, disturbance method, competence, controls and clearance evidence.
Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas that can create an occupational radiation risk.
Employers should assess radon risk in workplaces in relevant geographic areas or below ground.
Reliable measurement is needed where screening indicates that elevated levels may occur.
Measurements should represent occupied areas and suitable monitoring periods.
Results should be compared with applicable workplace action levels.
Engineering controls such as ventilation or sealing can reduce radon concentrations.
Work patterns and access may need control while remediation is planned.
Monitoring should be repeated after remediation or material building changes.
A radon map category or single short-term reading does not establish workplace exposure.
Conclusions require location, occupancy, detector placement, monitoring duration, seasonal context, results and remediation evidence.
Employers must provide adequate and appropriate first-aid equipment, facilities and people.
A first-aid needs assessment should reflect workplace hazards and workforce circumstances.
Arrangements should consider work patterns, remoteness, travel and shared premises.
An appointed person should take charge when a trained first-aider is not required.
First-aiders should have training appropriate to the assessed needs.
First-aid equipment should be suitably located, stocked and accessible.
Workers should be informed about first-aid arrangements.
Arrangements should be reviewed after changes, incidents or evidence that provision is inadequate.
A stocked first-aid box or named first-aider does not prove that provision is adequate for every shift.
Conclusions require hazards, headcount, shifts, location, training, response time, equipment and incident evidence.
RIDDOR requires responsible persons to report specified work-related deaths, injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences.
Not every accident or absence from work is reportable.
Reportability depends on the event, outcome, work connection and legal category.
Specified injuries to workers are reportable.
Over-seven-day incapacitation can be reportable within the required time.
Certain occupational diseases are reportable when diagnosed and linked to work.
Specified dangerous occurrences and certain gas incidents are reportable.
Records should be retained and reports submitted through the appropriate HSE route.
An accident-book entry or lost-time figure does not by itself determine RIDDOR reportability.
Conclusions require event date, person, outcome, diagnosis, incapacity period, work connection and legal-category evidence.
